cosy-lesson.title: "The longer we keep our inner child alive, the longer we keep the natural gifts we were born with.": Alisa Freindlich

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Inner child – a person's childhood self, especially regarded as an active part of their adult personality.

p.em: Example: Playing with blocks helps adults connect with their inner child.

cosy-blockquote.p: Natural – existing in or caused by nature; not made by humans.

p.em: Example: Her love for singing is a natural ability.

cosy-blockquote.p: Talent – a natural ability to do something well.

p.em: Example: Drawing beautiful pictures is a great artistic talent.

cosy-blockquote.p: Alive – living, active, or full of energy.

p.em: Example: Doing interesting sports makes me feel alive.

cosy-blockquote.p: Gift – a natural ability or talent.

p.em: Example: He has a special gift for learning languages easily.

cosy-blockquote.p: Preserve – to keep something in its original, safe state.

p.em: Example: We must preserve our childhood toys and memories.

cosy-blockquote.p: Curiosity – a strong desire to know or learn something new.

p.em: Example: Childhood curiosity makes learning very easy and fun.

cosy-blockquote.p: Sincerity – the quality of being honest and real.

p.em: Example: Children speak with absolute sincerity and tell the truth.

cosy-blockquote.p: Imagination – the ability to think of new and creative ideas.

p.em: Example: Reading books helps to grow your creative imagination.

cosy-blockquote.p: Wonder – a feeling of surprise and admiration for beautiful things.

p.em: Example: The starry night sky filled the children with wonder.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
How can adults protect and keep their inner child happy in a busy city?
★ What is one activity from your childhood that you still love doing today?

Why is it important to live in a natural environment to feel relaxed?
★ Do you prefer walking in a quiet forest or visiting a busy shopping mall?

Do you believe that everyone is born with a special talent for something?
★ What is a simple talent you have that you are proud of?

How does playing with children make adults feel happy and alive?
★ When was the last time you felt completely full of energy and alive?

Is a natural gift like drawing more important than practicing hard?
★ What special gift or skill do you want to learn next?

How do we preserve our childhood friendships and good memories?
※ Do you still talk to your friends from elementary school?

Why do some schools stop encouraging curiosity in growing children?
★ What is something you are very curious about learning today?

Why is absolute sincerity so common in young children and rare in adults?
★ Do you find it easy to say exactly what you are thinking to others?

How can we use our imagination to solve daily problems at work?
★ Did you have a very active imagination when you were a child?

How does looking at the ocean fill our minds with a sense of wonder?
★ What was the most beautiful natural view you saw last year?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: collaborative task or visual analysis in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, work together on the following task:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: 1-on-1 guided visual description and task response with teacher.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Look at the prompt and discuss your response with your teacher:

cosy-blockquote.p: A comparative reflection on our habits and self-perceptions.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In the future, we will have virtual reality games to help seniors re-experience their inner child. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you use a machine to see your childhood house as it was years ago?

Modern high-tech cities will eventually destroy our connection with natural forests. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you think we will live in cities with no real trees in 100 years?

Future schools will test babies at birth to identify their genetic talent. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you want to know your baby's genetic skills at birth?

Without art and creative hobbies, human beings are not truly alive. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you think practicing art is essential for a happy lifestyle?

A natural gift will always be more valuable than computer-calculated skills. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you value human-made paintings more than AI-made images?

It is impossible to preserve your childhood personality when you have a busy desk job. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Does your current job let you express your true creative self?

As we grow older, our natural curiosity is replaced by social duties. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you think adults are less curious than children?

Social media makes it very difficult to speak with absolute sincerity online. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you share your real feelings or only your best moments on social networks?

Artificial intelligence will eventually replace the human imagination in writing books. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you read a novel if it was written entirely by an AI?

A world fully governed by logic will have no space left for the wonder of mystery. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you think a world with zero mysteries would be boring?

ul.li: Incorrect: We are keep our inner child. → Correct: We keep our inner child / are keeping our inner child. ((Underlined error: auxiliary 'are' should not be used with base verb 'keep'))
Incorrect: I am agree with Voltaire. → Correct: I agree with Voltaire. ((Underlined error: 'agree' is a verb, do not use it with auxiliary 'am'))

Incorrect: Her talent is very beautifully. → Correct: Her talent is very beautiful. ((Underlined error: use the adjective 'beautiful' after the linking verb 'is' rather than the adverb 'beautifully'))

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Reflection & Feedback: Review language highlights and key corrections with your teacher.
